claims.assessment: uneasy that north-facing prostration by princes and first-rank clansmen, with only a joined-hands return bow, breached elder-junior kinship duty

claims.statement: Tang New Year ritual required descending the steps to greet uncles and returning bows to assembled officials, and had no protocol for consorts, princesses, and titled women to audience with the crown prince; cited as Tang precedent, not as Jin activity in the Tang dynasty.

translationRepairs: The investiture envoy stepped forward, took position to the right, and declared: "His Majesty has an edict."
The investiture envoy stepped forward, took position to the right, and declared: "There is an edict."
The announcement is 有制, the ritual formula that an edict is present; the original invents His Majesty, which is not in this clause.

After setting the book-and-seal couches to east and west, each bearer descended by the side halls and went directly out the hall gate behind the Secretariat director and others, to await re-entry, then carried the book and seal into the inner palace.

After setting the book-and-seal couches to east and west, each bearer descended by the side halls and went directly out the hall gate behind the Palace Attendant and others, to await re-entry, then carried the book and seal into the inner palace.
The bearers exit 于侍中等班後, behind the Palace Attendant's formation; 中書令 appears in the preceding unit, not here.
Two days after receiving investiture, inner attendants set up a seat in her residential hall, facing south.
Two days after the empress received investiture, inner attendants set up a seat in her residential hall, facing south.
The source names 皇后 as the one who had received investiture; the original drops that title and leaves the recipient unspecified.

Protocol secretaries and Court of Imperial Sacrifices academicians directed the procession; the director went ahead as guide; book-escort officers led the book forward, followed in order by the Grand Commandant, Secretariat director, book-bearers, and others.

Protocol secretaries and Court of Imperial Sacrifices academicians directed the procession; the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices went ahead as guide; book-escort officers led the book forward, followed in order by the Grand Commandant, Secretariat director, book-bearers, and others.
太常卿 is the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices leading the procession; 'the director' is ambiguous beside the later Secretariat director.

Protocol secretaries and academicians directed the procession; the director led the way as book-escort officers carried the book up to music, followed by the Grand Commandant and others, advancing to the cushioned station before both empress dowagers, where the music stopped.

Protocol secretaries and academicians directed the procession; the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices led the way as book-escort officers carried the book up to music, followed by the Grand Commandant and others, advancing to the cushioned station before both empress dowagers, where the music stopped.
Again 太常卿 names the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; reducing him to 'the director' conceals the office.

Protocol secretaries led the Grand Preceptor up the western steps to prostrate himself, kneel, and report: "The civil and military officials, officers of record, your subjects [names], bow the head and state: under the empress dowagers' exalted reception of the investiture book, may imperial nurture be secure. We pray for blessings and longevity equal to Heaven.

Protocol secretaries led the Grand Preceptor up the western steps to prostrate himself, kneel, and report: "The civil and military officials, officers of record, your subjects [names], bow the head and state: under the empress dowager's exalted reception of the investiture book, may the emperor's nurture be forever secure.
皇太后殿下 is singular; 永安帝養 is a wish that the emperor's nurture remain forever secure; 仰祈福壽 belongs to the next unit.

The protocol secretaries led the Grand Preceptor to ascend the western steps, prostrate himself, kneel and memorialize: "The civil and military hundred officials, officers of record, your subjects so-and-so, bow the head and state: under the empress dowagers' exalted reception of the book ceremony, may imperial nurture be secure. We look up and pray for blessing and longevity equal to Heaven.

The protocol secretaries led the Grand Preceptor to ascend the western steps, prostrate himself, kneel and memorialize: "The civil and military hundred officials, officers of record, your subjects so-and-so, bow the head and state: under the empress dowager's exalted reception of the book ceremony, may the emperor's nurture be forever secure.
The literal likewise pluralizes 皇太后殿下, under-translates 永安帝養, and imports 仰祈福壽 from s0196.

Inner and outer consorts all bowed twice; the Director of the Inner Palace received the command, descended by the western steps, and stood east of the consorts facing east; the master of announcements said: "Bow twice."

Inner and outer consorts all bowed twice; the Director of the Inner Palace received the command, descended by the western steps, and stood north of the consorts facing east; the master of announcements said: "Bow twice."
於命婦之北東向立 places the Director north of the consorts, facing east, not east of the consorts.
The emperor came forth from the eastern sequence, took the imperial seat, incense smoke rose, the fans opened, the curtain was rolled up, and the music ceased.
The emperor came forth from the eastern side-chamber, took the imperial seat, incense smoke rose, the fans opened, the curtain was rolled up, and the music ceased.
東序 is the eastern side-chamber of the hall, not a 'sequence'.

Protocol secretaries and academicians led the Secretariat director to the reading station; the vice director set the book case before him; the book-bearer knelt facing west and presented it; the crown prince knelt; when reading was finished he prostrated himself and rose.

Protocol secretaries and erudites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices led the Secretariat director to the reading station; the vice director set the book case before him; the book-bearer knelt facing west and presented it; the crown prince knelt; when reading was finished he prostrated himself and rose.
太常博士 are erudites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, not academicians.

The protocol secretaries and Court of Imperial Sacrifices academicians led the Director of the Secretariat to the position for reading the book; the Vice Director of the Secretariat led the book case and set it before him; the book-presentation official knelt facing west and presented it; the crown prince knelt; when the reading was finished he prostrated himself and rose.

The protocol secretaries and erudites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices led the Director of the Secretariat to the position for reading the book; the Vice Director of the Secretariat led the book case and set it before him; the book-presentation official knelt facing west and presented it; the crown prince knelt; when the reading was finished he prostrated himself and rose.
The literal likewise renders 太常博士 as academicians; erudites is the office name.

Next the protocol secretaries and Court of Imperial Sacrifices academicians led the Palace Attendant to the position for presenting the seal; the Vice Director of the Chancellery led the seal case and stood to his right; the Palace Attendant reverently presented the seal to the crown prince; the crown prince tucked the jade tablet, knelt and received it, handed it to the Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent; the Left Guardian knelt and received it; the crown prince prostrated himself and rose; the Left Guardian raised the seal, rose, and placed it on the couch; the Palace Attendant and those below withdrew and returned to their original formation.

Next the protocol secretaries and erudites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices led the Palace Attendant to the position for presenting the seal; the Vice Director of the Chancellery led the seal case and stood to his right; the Palace Attendant reverently presented the seal to the crown prince; the crown prince tucked the jade tablet, knelt and received it, handed it to the Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent; the Left Guardian knelt and received it; the crown prince prostrated himself and rose; the Left Guardian raised the seal, rose, and placed it on the couch; the Palace Attendant and those below withdrew and returned to their original formation.
This unit also has 太常博士 leading the Palace Attendant; they are erudites, not academicians.

The inner attendants, receiving the command, requested the fans; the fans closed; the curtain was lowered; the whip was cracked; music played; the emperor descended from the seat and entered by the western sequence back to the rear pavilion; escort was as on the outward journey; the fans opened and the music ceased.

The inner attendants, receiving the command, requested the fans; the fans closed; the curtain was lowered; the whip was cracked; music played; the emperor descended from the seat and entered by the western side-chamber back to the rear pavilion; escort was as on the outward journey; the fans opened and the music ceased.
西序 is the western side-chamber, not a 'sequence'.
The emperor came forth from the eastern sequence, took his seat, and the curtain was rolled up.
The emperor came forth from the eastern side-chamber, took his seat, and the curtain was rolled up.
東序 is again the eastern side-chamber, not a sequence.
The fans closed; the whip was cracked; he entered by the western sequence and returned to the rear pavilion; escort was as on the outward journey.
The fans closed; the whip was cracked; he entered by the western side-chamber and returned to the rear pavilion; escort was as on the outward journey.
入西序 names the western side-chamber, not a sequence.
When drinking was finished they received the cup, returned to position, handed the terrace to the officiants, and bowed twice.

They first bowed twice; two pavilion commissioners together bowed with joined hands and entered inside the railing, bowed and knelt; when the benediction was finished they bowed in place, rose, returned to position, bowed twice, bowed twice again, advanced wine at the terrace, withdrew and knelt.
The original English belongs to 候飲畢接盞; this unit is 先再拜, two 閣使 entering the railing, the benediction, and 棲台進酒.
They awaited the drinking to be finished, received the cup, returned to position, turned the terrace over to the officiants, and bowed twice.

First they bowed twice; two pavilion commissioners together bowed with joined hands and entered inside the railing, bowed and knelt; when the blessing was finished they bowed in place, rose, returned to position, bowed twice, bowed twice again, advanced wine at the terrace, withdrew and knelt.
The literal is shifted one unit later and omits 先再拜、二閣使、祝畢, and 棲台進酒.

The Xuanhui Commissioner brought wine; the emperor personally bestowed it; they received the cup, withdrew slightly, knelt and drank; when finished the commissioner received the cup; they returned to position and bowed twice.
When drinking was finished they received the cup, returned to position, handed the terrace to the officiants, and bowed twice.
候飲畢，接盞，復位，轉臺與執事者 names receiving the cup and handing over the terrace, not the Xuanhui Commissioner or an imperial gift of wine.

The Xuanhui Commissioner advanced with wine; the emperor personally bestowed wine; they received the cup, withdrew slightly and knelt to drink; when finished the Xuanhui Commissioner received the cup; they returned to position and bowed twice.
They awaited the drinking to be finished, received the cup, returned to position, turned the terrace over to the officiants, and bowed twice.
The literal invents 宣徽使 and 皇帝親賜酒, which first appear in the next unit.

Again they bowed with joined hands, entered the railing, knelt and tucked their tablets, received the bestowed objects, rose, returned to position, bowed twice, withdrew to change clothes, entered the hall slightly east, and stood facing west.

The Xuanhui Commissioner brought wine; the emperor personally bestowed it; they received the cup, withdrew slightly, knelt and drank; when finished the commissioner received the cup; they returned to position and bowed twice.
This unit is 宣徽使以酒進，皇帝親賜酒; the original English translates the following 複揖入欄子內 clause instead.

Again they bowed with joined hands and entered inside the railing, knelt and tucked their tablets, received the bestowed objects; when finished they withdrew their tablets, rose, returned to position, bowed twice, withdrew to change clothes, entered the hall slightly to the east, and stood facing west.

The Xuanhui Commissioner advanced with wine; the emperor personally bestowed wine; they received the cup, withdrew slightly and knelt to drink; when finished the Xuanhui Commissioner received the cup; they returned to position and bowed twice.
The literal is shifted to the next unit and omits both 宣徽使 and 皇帝.
Imperial consorts advanced birthday wine; the crown prince knelt; the consorts also knelt; when drinking was finished each bowed twice again.

Again they bowed with joined hands, entered the railing, knelt and tucked their tablets, received the bestowed objects, rose, returned to position, bowed twice, withdrew to change clothes, entered the hall slightly east, and stood facing west.
複揖入欄子內，跪搢笏，受賜物 is a second entry to receive gifts, not consorts advancing birthday wine.
Imperial consorts and the like advanced wine to encourage the birthday celebration; the crown prince knelt; the imperial consorts also knelt; when the drinking was finished each again bowed twice.

Again they bowed with joined hands and entered inside the railing, knelt and tucked their tablets, received the bestowed objects; when finished they withdrew their tablets, rose, returned to position, bowed twice, withdrew to change clothes, entered the hall slightly to the east, and stood facing west.
The literal renders 皇妃等進勸生日酒, which is the following unit, not this one.
For officials' congratulations, at dawn that day all gathered outside the gate in official dress; the Junior Guardian memorialized: "Request that the inner court be secured."
Imperial consorts advanced birthday wine; the crown prince knelt; the consorts also knelt; when drinking was finished each bowed twice again.
皇妃等進勸生日酒，皇太子跪 names consorts and the kneeling crown prince; the original is a duplicate of the 群官致賀 sentence.

When the assembled officials offered congratulations, on that day at dawn all wore official dress and gathered outside the gate; the Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent memorialized: "Request the inner court be made strict."
Imperial consorts and the like advanced wine to encourage the birthday celebration; the crown prince knelt; the imperial consorts also knelt; when the drinking was finished each again bowed twice.
The literal belongs to 群官致賀，則其日質明, not to this consorts-and-wine unit.
In the seventh year it was fixed that when the crown prince attended court he might meet imperial princes and chief ministers, while other officials and clansmen withdrew.
This was what had been established in Dading 2.
The unit is only 大定二年所定也; the seventh-year court-meeting rule is the next sentence.

In the seventh year a fixed protocol was established: when the crown prince attended court he was permitted to meet imperial princes and chief ministers; other officials and imperial clansmen all withdrew.
It was what had been determined in the second year of Dading.
The literal invents 七年定制 content that is absent from this unit.
Later he was also permitted to meet the Bureau of Military Affairs deputies, the Censor-in-Chief, the Director of the Imperial Clan Court, and the Eastern Palace Three Preceptors.
In the seventh year it was fixed that when the crown prince attended court he might meet imperial princes and chief ministers, while other officials and clansmen withdrew.
七年，定制，皇太子赴朝，許與親王宰執相見 is the Dading 7 restriction; the original English is the later 後亦許 clause.
Later he was also permitted to meet the deputy commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs, the Censor-in-Chief, the Director of the Imperial Clan Court, and the Eastern Palace Three Preceptors.

In the seventh year a fixed protocol was established: when the crown prince attended court he was permitted to meet imperial princes and chief ministers; other officials and imperial clansmen all withdrew.
The literal skips 七年定制 and instead translates the following 後亦許 list of offices.

In the ninth year it was fixed that whenever the crown prince went out, a cushioned station was set three li outside the capital gate; the Three Excellencies, chief ministers, and those below in official dress stood in double rows; the crown prince in ordinary dress; they bowed the body; the lead official said: "May the Eastern Palace enjoy ten thousand blessings."

Later he was also permitted to meet the Bureau of Military Affairs commissioners and deputy commissioners, the Censor-in-Chief, the Director of the Imperial Clan Court, and the Eastern Palace Three Preceptors.
後亦許與樞密使副、御史大夫、判宗正、東宮三師相見 is a later audience permission, not the ninth-year capital-gate rite.

In the ninth year a fixed protocol was established: whenever the crown prince went out, a cushioned position was set three li outside the capital gate; the Three Excellencies, chief ministers, and those below in official dress stood in double rows; the crown prince in ordinary dress; the Three Excellencies, chief ministers, and those below bowed the body; the head of the formation offered words: "May the Eastern Palace enjoy ten thousand blessings."

Later he was also permitted to meet the commissioners and deputy commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs, the Censor-in-Chief, the Director of the Imperial Clan Court, and the Eastern Palace Three Preceptors.
The original is the ninth-year outing protocol, so a real shift must be repaired; 樞密使副 is commissioner and deputy, not deputies alone.
